population.text: Adult patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma; efficacy population all triple-class exposed with a median of 5 prior lines of therapy (78% had at least 4 prior lines), 76% triple-class refractory

citations.quote: received a median of 5 prior lines of therapy (range 2 to 14); 78% of patients had at least 4 prior lines of therapy
All patients were triple-class exposed (i.e., received a prior PI, IMiD, and anti-CD38 mAb) and 76% were triple-class refractory.

endpoint.text: Overall response rate (ORR) assessed by an Independent Review Committee (IRC)

citations.quote: The primary efficacy endpoint was overall response rate (ORR) assessed by an Independent Review Committee (IRC).
Patients in the efficacy population (N=110) had a median age of 66 years

result.text: ORR 61.8% (95% CI: 52.1, 70.9); median DOR not reached; estimated DOR rate 90.6% at 6 months and 66.5% at 9 months

citations.quote: The ORR in the efficacy population was 61.8% (95% CI: 52.1, 70.9).
the median duration of response (DOR) was not reached (95% CI: 9.0, not estimable), and the estimated DOR rate was 90.6% (95% CI: 80.3, 95.7) at 6 months and 66.5% (95% CI: 38.8, 83.9) at 9 months.

indication.text: TECVAYLI is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma who have received at least four prior lines of therapy, including a proteasome inhibitor, an immunomodulatory agent and an anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody.

citations.quote: TECVAYLI is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma who have received at least four prior lines of therapy, including a proteasome inhibitor, an immunomodulatory agent and an anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody.

target_moa.text: Teclistamab is a bispecific BCMA-directed and CD3-directed antibody that binds BCMA on multiple myeloma cells and CD3 on T-cells, promoting T-cell dependent elimination of BCMA-expressing cells.

citations.quote: Teclistamab is a first in class BCMA-directed CD3 T-cell engaging bispecific monoclonal antibody.

Teclistamab binds BCMA and CD3 and promotes the T-cell dependent elimination of BCMA-expressing cells; the Established Pharmacologic Class of teclistamab is "bispecific B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA)-directed CD3 T-cell engager".
Teclistamab (also referred to as JNJ-64007957 or BCMB72) is an IgG4-based bispecific antibody (bsAb) construct directed against B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA) and CD3.

key_safety.text: Key safety concerns are cytokine release syndrome (CRS, 72%) and neurologic toxicity (57%), including ICANS (6%). Most common adverse reactions (>=20%) are pyrexia, cytokine release syndrome, musculoskeletal pain, injection site reaction, fatigue, upper respiratory tract infection, nausea, headache, pneumonia, and diarrhea.

citations.quote: CRS and neurologic toxicity were common, occurring in 72% and 57% of patients, respectively, treated with teclistamab at the recommended dose.
ICANS occurred in 6% of patients.

The most common adverse reactions (\ge 20\%) are pyrexia, cytokine release syndrome, musculoskeletal pain, injection site reaction, fatigue, upper respiratory tract infection, nausea, headache, pneumonia, and diarrhea.

detail.text: Boxed warning for Cytokine Release Syndrome (including life-threatening or fatal reactions) and Neurologic Toxicity including ICANS.

citations.quote: WARNING: CYTOKINE RELEASE SYNDROME and NEUROLOGIC TOXICITY including IMMUNE EFFECTOR CELL-ASSOCIATED NEUROTOXICITY SYNDROME
Cytokine release syndrome (CRS), including life-threatening or fatal reactions, can occur in patients receiving TECVAYLI.

detail.text: TECVAYLI is available only through a restricted program under a REMS with elements to assure safe use (ETASU) to mitigate the risks of CRS and neurologic toxicity, including ICANS.

citations.quote: TECVAYLI is available only through a restricted program called the TECVAYLI Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS). (5.3)

we have also determined that Tecvayli (teclistamab-cqyv) can be approved only if elements necessary to assure safe use are required as part of the REMS to mitigate the risks of CRS and neurologic toxicity, including ICANS, listed in the labeling of the drug.
